chunks: And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) used to say: 'I love to be constant in worship, even if it is little.' We said: 'Do you make up the night prayer during the day while traveling?' He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.صَلَاةَ اللَّيْلِ: night prayer (specifically the voluntary night prayer)

ai.seo_question: How should a traveler maintain their night prayer if they cannot pray it at night?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sajjad (AS) emphasizes the spiritual merit of *istiqarah* (consistency), prioritizing the regularity of practice over its volume, a principle highly valued in Shia asceticism. It specifically clarifies the flexibility for travelers to perform *Qada al-Layl* (the night prayer) during daylight hours, demonstrating the practical adaptability of devotional acts within the jurisprudential framework of Shaykh al-Tusi.
